clue.text: Breakfast inside?

explanation.surface: A question about a morning meal eaten indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is British slang for in prison, and doing time there is called 'doing porridge'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oat gruel is a classic morning meal, and in British slang the word also means a stretch served in jail.

clue.text: Say please, or something like it: that's the law

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the word aloud and hear what it resembles

parts.note: the word please, spoken quickly with the first vowel swallowed

explanation.surface: Someone notes that asking politely amounts to legal authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or something like it' admits the sound match is loose: POLICE said quickly as 'p'leece' is close to please.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The law' is informal for the constabulary, the officers who enforce it.

clue.text: Let the public know about the calves we eat

parts.note: re means about or concerning
veal is the meat of calves

explanation.surface: Disclosing to the public the truth about the calves in our diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose something is to make it known to everyone.

clue.text: Had a pub meal it was instinctive

parts.note: an inn is a pub
had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: Someone eats at the local without thinking, purely by habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Had a pub meal' as ATE in an INN, which gives INN then ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inborn comes naturally, without being learned, which is what instinctive means.

clue.text: Eco-friendly firm has an effect

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly
a house is a business firm, as in a publishing house

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded company makes an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: it is the glasshouse that gave its name to the greenhouse effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass building for plants names the warming effect of gases trapping heat in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Too sluggish to move tripod?

indicators.note: moving the letters of the three-legged stand rearranges them into a new word

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is too lethargic to shift a camera stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor is inactivity, so someone so sluggish cannot stir.

clue.text: Estimate too highly-put- ting on the spinners will improve it

definitions.text: put- ting on the spinners will improve it

explanation.surface: Overvaluing something, while a cricket captain brings on slow bowlers to speed things up.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the 'over rate' is how many overs are bowled per hour; spin bowlers have short run-ups, so bringing them on raises it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overvalue is to rate too high; in cricket the pace of play, overs per hour, rises when slow bowlers are used.

clue.text: Hair for a fly-whisk?

parts.note: the hairstyle is named after the swishing hair a small horse uses to brush off flies

explanation.surface: Asking what hair might serve to swat flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle gathered at the back resembles the swishing hind hair of a small horse.

clue.text: Don't copy lamb if you're mutton, it's horse work!

definitions.text: Don't copy lamb if you're mutton

explanation.surface: Advice to older people not to dress young, oddly tied to horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase 'mutton dressed as lamb' mocks an older person dressing young; the advice is to DRESS your AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing in keeping with your years is the advice to the 'mutton'; it is also the training of a horse in precise movements.

clue.text: Shrub to finish in seaweed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the seaweed word

parts.note: laver is an edible seaweed
end means to finish

explanation.surface: Instructions to close out a planting in seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fragrant purple-flowered plant is a small woody bush.

clue.text: In which to materialise ancestors?

indicators.note: in points to letters lying inside the clue's words materialise ancestors

explanation.surface: Asking where one might make forebears appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritualist meeting is where the dead are said to be called up.

clue.text: Freewheeling variety of agnostic

indicators.note: a variety of the word gives another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Describing a casual, uncommitted kind of doubter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving without power, as a cyclist does downhill, is freewheeling.

clue.text: Deserter detained by soldiers goes free

indicators.note: detained by means held inside the soldiers' letters

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier is held by troops but released.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given at no charge costs nothing.

clue.text: An agreement to love what is small in old age

parts.note: a nod signals agreement
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
mini means small

explanation.surface: Agreeing to love something little in one's later years.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin for 'in the year of the Lord', the phrase is also used to mean advanced age.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin dating term is used informally for advancing years, the toll of time.

clue.text: Free, not good if good

explanation.surface: A paradox about something costless being bad if it is good.
explanation.walkthrough: Put 'good' in front of the answer and it becomes 'good-for-nothing', meaning not good.
explanation.definitionFit: Costing nothing means free; preceded by 'good', the phrase describes a worthless idler.

clue.text: Prepare to read one who is transparent

explanation.surface: Getting ready to read about a person who hides nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: You part the covers of a volume before reading; a person easy to understand is said to be like one.

clue.text: Cow hit below the forehead?

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts the hitting word under the forehead word

parts.note: the brow is the forehead
beat means hit

explanation.surface: A cow struck beneath its forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, to bully into submission.

clue.text: Where in paper the election of officers etc gets bogged down?

definitions.text: Where in paper the election of officers etc gets bogged down?

indicators.note: in places the meeting inside the paper word

parts.note: a quire is a quantity of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
an AGM, annual general meeting, is where officers are elected

explanation.surface: Asking where, in the newspaper, coverage of a society's elections gets stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or marsh is where you get stuck, and so a messy situation.

clue.text: Jane Austen's creed?

explanation.surface: A question about the beliefs of the novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of her last completed novel, and a religious belief or denomination is also so called.

clue.text: Crow heard sound of steam train

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is identified by how it sounds

parts.note: a steam locomotive goes chuff

explanation.surface: A bird hears a steam engine puffing.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-billed bird is a member of the corvid family.

clue.text: One who rolled out the barrels starts working with others

definitions.text: One who rolled out the barrels

indicators.note: only the start of the word for working together is used

parts.note: cooperates means works with others

explanation.surface: A barrel-roller begins working as part of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll Out the Barrel' is a well-known song; the barrel-maker rolls out barrels he has made.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel-maker produces casks, the trade being coopering.

clue.text: Opposition had outside broadcast

indicators.note: outside means the broadcast word wraps around had

parts.note: to sow is to broadcast seed

explanation.surface: The opposition party had an outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the 'shadow cabinet' is the opposition's team of would-be ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's frontbench team in Britain is called the shadow cabinet.

clue.text: Waste to change poles? Is this the Millennium?

indicators.note: swapping one pole for the other changes south to north in the waste word

parts.note: sewage is waste

explanation.surface: Wondering if turning the world's waste around heralds the millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: The year 2000 was hailed by some as the dawn of a new spiritual era.

clue.text: Bears an expression of disdain

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear
a second Pooh bear, since bears is plural

explanation.surface: Bears are scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something scornfully, or the exclamation used in scorn.

clue.text: Single drink for Eugene

parts.note: single means one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A lone drink for a man called Eugene.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene is the first name of Pushkin's title character.

clue.text: Copper's relation in attempt to buy a tooth

indicators.note: in places the copper pieces inside the bid word

parts.note: a bid is an offer to buy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive
pi is the ratio, or relation, of a circle's circumference to its diameter

explanation.surface: A policeman's relative tries to buy a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A premolar with two points is a type of tooth.

clue.text: Little furry creature to supply clothes for a number

parts.note: to kit out is to equip with clothes
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Providing outfits for a number of small furry animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is small and furry.

clue.text: Retreat not devoid of attraction

parts.note: not lacking something means being with it
a draw is an attraction, as a big name draws a crowd

explanation.surface: Retreat, though not without appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull back is to retreat.
